title: Non-exchangeable Conformal Prediction for Temporal Graph Neural Networks

problem.claim: Temporal dependencies in graph structure, node attributes, and ground-truth labels violate the exchangeability assumption used by standard conformal prediction methods.

gap.claim: Existing conformal prediction methods for GNNs predominantly focus on static graphs and do not address evolving real-world graphs.

contributions.claim: NCPNET is an end-to-end conformal prediction framework tailored for temporal graphs.
The framework uses a diffusion-based non-conformity score capturing topological and temporal uncertainties in evolving networks.
An efficiency-aware optimization algorithm improves computational efficiency and reduces coverage violations in the conformal prediction process.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe NCPNET as a novel framework for temporal graphs.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report extensive experiments on WIKI, REDDIT, DBLP, and IBM Anti-Money Laundering temporal-graph datasets.
The authors report guaranteed coverage in temporal graphs and up to a 31% reduction in prediction set size on WIKI.
The authors report improved efficiency compared with state-of-the-art methods and make the data and code available.

narrative_sequence.summary: Conformal prediction can quantify uncertainty and improve GNN reliability in high-stakes applications.
Existing methods focus mainly on static graphs, while temporal dependencies violate standard exchangeability assumptions.
The paper introduces NCPNET, extending conformal prediction to dynamic settings with a diffusion-based non-conformity score.
An efficiency-aware optimization algorithm targets computational efficiency and coverage violations.
Experiments on diverse real-world temporal graphs report coverage, prediction-set-size, and efficiency results, with data and code availability.

source_observation.claim: Temporal dependencies can invalidate exchangeability assumptions underlying standard conformal prediction.

interpretation.claim: Uncertainty methods may need explicit adaptation when data-generating structure evolves over time.

application.claim: For temporal graph prediction, consider modeling both temporal and topological uncertainty in the non-conformity score.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the conditions under which the reported coverage guarantees hold.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the prediction task, model architecture, or evaluation protocol.
The abstract does not provide baseline identities, numerical coverage values, or results beyond the reported WIKI reduction.
The abstract does not detail the theoretical assumptions or proof of the coverage guarantee.
